name: Linear Dilaton Vacuum
description: A spacetime that is flat in the string frame, with a dilaton falling linearly in time, and expands in proportion to time in the Einstein frame.
convention: We use units in which the speed of light is one.
history: Flat spacetime admits a dilaton that varies from event to event. The dilaton $\Phi$ sets the string coupling $g_s = e^\Phi$ [angius2022linear]. Robert C. Myers constructed a string background in arbitrary spacetime dimensions in 1987 with a dilaton linear in the coordinates [angius2022linear, myers1987linear]. When the central charge balances, a timelike linear dilaton defines a worldsheet theory conformal to all orders in the string length squared [angius2022linear, aharony2007linear].¶Take four uncompactified dimensions, in units where the speed of light is one. Additional degrees of freedom can contribute to the central charge [devega1994linear, aharony2007linear]. In the string frame, the line element is $ds_S^2 = -d\eta^2 + d\mathbf{x}^2$ and the dilaton is $\Phi = -q\eta$ [devega1994linear, angius2022linear]. Here $\eta$ is time, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes Cartesian spatial coordinates, and $q > 0$ has units of inverse length. The Einstein frame uses $g^E_{\mu\nu} = e^{-2\Phi}g^S_{\mu\nu}$ [angius2022linear]. The two frames describe the same background.¶With cosmic time $\tau = e^{q\eta}/q$, its line element is $ds_E^2 = -d\tau^2 + q^2\tau^2 d\mathbf{x}^2$ [devega1994linear, angius2022linear]. Its flat spatial slices expand in proportion to $\tau$, and its Ricci scalar is $R = 6/\tau^2$. As $\tau$ approaches zero, the curvature diverges and the string coupling grows without bound [angius2022linear].¶Ignatios Antoniadis, Constantin Bachas, John R. Ellis, and Dimitri V. Nanopoulos found "only two discrete classes" of Robertson-Walker string cosmologies without dynamic matter in 1988: "static Einstein universes and linearly expanding Milne universes" [antoniadis1988cosmology]. The Milne universe and this Einstein frame universe both expand linearly; the Milne universe has negatively curved spatial slices and is flat as a spacetime. Linearly expanding homogeneous and isotropic universes also arise in bosonic, heterotic, and type II string theories [antoniadis1989expanding].¶A dilaton that varies along a spatial direction also accompanies a flat string frame [angius2022linear]. Far from Edward Witten's two dimensional black hole the string frame approaches a flat metric and the dilaton is linear in the spatial coordinate [karananas2021linear, mandal1991]. Georgios K. Karananas, Alex Kehagias, and John Taskas found a four dimensional black hole with a planar horizon whose string frame contains Witten's two dimensional hole [karananas2021linear]. The throat of the extreme magnetically charged dilaton black hole also carries a dilaton linear in distance [giddings1992].
